A brief history of humanity's most important technology
Before money, there was barter. And barter had a
Someone with eggs who wants bread
Not by design. Not by decree.

Money has never had to come from the government — in fact, until recently it never did. Throughout history, humans have converged on money naturally, through free market competition. People gravitate toward whichever good best fulfills the roles of money — what economists call the
: the item most easily exchanged for anything else.
— through practical necessity and market consensus, not by design or decree.
Each step solved a shortcoming of the previous one.
Every monetary form we’ll see was an improvement on the last — until it wasn’t. The story of money is humanity’s ongoing search for a better carrier of value.
Direct exchange of goods for goods.
The earliest form of human trade.
Required the double coincidence of wants. Couldn’t scale beyond small communities.
Shells, beads, salt, cattle — the first widely accepted stores of value.
Crossed the double-coincidence barrier — anyone would accept them.
Not scarce enough. New technology (glass beads, mass harvesting) could inflate the supply overnight.
Gold and silver emerged through global trade competition.
Heavy. Hard to transport in large amounts. Difficult to subdivide for small transactions.
Easier to carry, divide, and transact.
Kept the gold anchor — supply constrained.
Required trust in the issuer to actually hold the gold and honor redemptions.
Rigid monetary supply limited governments and central banks in their spending and flexibility to manage the economy.
Fiat (government-decreed) removed gold constraint, allowing for easier expansion or contraction of money supply.
Unlimited supply can lead to inflation or currency debasement — requires deep trust.
Bitcoin introduces digital scarcity, decentralization, censorship resistance, and trustless global value transfer.
Seeks to combine the best traits of gold's scarcity with the portability and divisibility of fiat, without needing centralized issuers.
Now we know where money came from.

Fiat fails the most important function.
Inflation silently erodes the purchasing power of fiat currencies every year.
The US dollar has lost over 85% of its purchasing power since 1971.
People intuitively know this — which is why they don't use fiat as a true store of value.
Everyone is forced to become an investor — not because they want to, but because saving in fiat is no longer safe.
Store of value is the foundation.

Retains purchasing power over time. Bitcoin is currently emerging as the new store of value of the digital age.

Every monetary good in history that emerged organically followed this pattern. This applies to money that emerges naturally through free market competition by being selected by the people — not to currency, which the government essentially forces us to use.
People start collecting something because it's beautiful, rare, novel, or carries status.
As more people start collecting it, demand rises and so does its purchasing power.
Once enough people collect something, it will be recognised as a means of keeping and storing value.
Purchasing power rises as more people demand it, until it plateaus when widely held.
Once purchasing power stabilises, a money can be used as a medium of exchange.
This may take decades or centuries.
Once a money is widely used as a medium of exchange, goods will be priced in it.
Bitcoin is transitioning from collectible to store of value.
Bitcoin has graduated from a niche collectible to a recognised monetary asset.
Increasingly held by institutions, corporations, and even nation-states.
Still completing its transition into a credible store of value — purchasing power has been volatile but trending up across multi-year cycles.
Medium of exchange and unit of account are stages still ahead.
This is why critics who say "I can't buy my coffee with Bitcoin" miss the point. Bitcoin isn't supposed to be a medium of exchange yet — it's still completing the foundation.
Skipping straight to medium of exchange before establishing store of value is what fiat does.
